subject: health
title: Sun and Water Safety
about: Sunscreen and putting more on, hats and sunglasses, shade and water on hot days, what to do if he feels too hot, never swimming alone, a grown-up water watcher, life jackets before the boat, staying out of water with no grown-up around, and checking how deep before jumping in. NC 1.PCH.2.1 (situations that can cause injury) with 1.PCH.1.4 (dress for the weather) and 1.NPA.1.1 (reasons to drink water); builds on Safe Outside for summer.
tip: Make him the sunscreen helper: he squeezes the dot and names the spots we always forget, like ears and the back of the neck.

cards.q: Sunscreen keeps your skin safe from what?
cards.note: A sunburn is red, hot and sore. Sunscreen blocks the sun's rays so skin does not burn.

cards.q: When do you put sunscreen on?
cards.note: Put it on about 15 minutes before you go out so it has time to soak in.

cards.q: You have been swimming for a long time. What do you do with sunscreen?
cards.note: Water and sweat wash sunscreen away. Put more on every two hours and after swimming.

cards.q: What keeps the sun off your face, ears and neck?
cards.note: A wide brim shades the spots sunscreen misses.

cards.q: What protects your eyes from bright sun?
cards.note: Even on a cloudy day, the sun's rays can reach your eyes.

cards.q: It is very hot at the park. Where is a cool place to take a break?
cards.note: Under a tree, a tent or an umbrella. Shade can feel many degrees cooler.

cards.q: When is the sun the strongest?
cards.note: From late morning to late afternoon, look for shade and keep the hat on.

cards.q: You are playing hard on a hot day. When should you drink water?
cards.note: By the time you feel thirsty, your body already needs water. Sip before you get thirsty.

cards.q: You feel dizzy and much too hot while playing outside. What do you do?
cards.note: Stop, get to shade, sip water and tell a grown-up. Dizzy, sick or a headache in the heat means your body needs to cool down.

cards.q: You got too hot. What helps your body cool down?
cards.note: A cool wet cloth on your neck helps too.

cards.q: You are a good swimmer. Is it okay to swim all by yourself?
cards.note: Even great swimmers only swim when a grown-up is watching. That is the rule for everyone.

cards.q: A grown-up is the water watcher. What do they keep their eyes on?
cards.note: The water watcher does not read, text or chat. Eyes on the water the whole time.

cards.q: When do you put on your life jacket for a boat ride?
cards.note: It goes on at the dock and stays buckled until you are back on land.

cards.q: Which one is made to keep you safe in the water?
cards.note: Floaties and pool toys are for fun. Only a life jacket is made to keep you afloat.

cards.q: Before you jump into water, what does a grown-up check first?
cards.note: Jumping into shallow water can hurt your head. Feet first, and only where a grown-up says it is okay.

cards.q: Who sits in the tall chair and watches the swimmers at a pool or beach?
cards.note: The lifeguard's whistle means stop and listen. Your own grown-up still watches you too.

cards.q: The pool gate is shut. Do you open it by yourself?
cards.note: A pool fence and gate keep kids out until a grown-up is ready to watch.

cards.q: You find a pond or pool and no grown-up is around. What do you do?
cards.note: Water is only for when a grown-up is watching. Go find one first.
